Impact: prevent deadlock in NMI
The ring buffers are not yet totally lockless with writing to
the buffer. When a writer crosses a page
column2: it grabs a per cpu spinlock

column1: to protect against a reader. The spinlocks taken by a writer are not
to protect against other writers
column2: since a writer can only write to

column1: its own per cpu buffer. The spinlocks protect against readers that
can touch any cpu buffer. The writers are made to be reentrant
with the spinlocks disabling interrupts.
The problem arises when an NMI writes to the buffer
crosses a page boundary. If it grabs a spinlock
with another writer (since disabling interrupts does not protect
against NMIs) or with a reader on the same CPU. Luckily
users are not reentrant and protects against this issue. But if a
user of the ring buffer becomes reentrant (which is what the ring
buffers do allow)
column2: if the NMI also writes to the ring buffer then

column1: we risk the chance of a deadlock.
This patch moves the ftrace_nmi_enter called by nmi_enter() to the
ring buffer code. It replaces the current ftrace_nmi_enter that is
used by arch specific code to arch_ftrace_nmi_enter and updates
the Kconfig to handle it.
When an NMI is called
column2: it will set a per cpu variable in the ring buffer

column1: code and will clear it when the NMI exits. If a write to the ring buffer
crosses page boundaries inside an NMI
column2: a trylock is used on the spin

column1: lock instead. If the spinlock fails to be acquired
is discarded.
This bug appeared in the ftrace work in the RT tree
is reentrant. This workaround solved the deadlocks that appeared there.
